6.0.0.en: Yoke: a piece of wood placed on the necks of the two animals that draw farm implements, and it signifies slavery, that is, that slaves are under the authority of their masters.

6.0.1.en: Without attacking the institution of slavery, the Apostle dealt with its problem by lifting the morale of the slaves and giving them guidance for a godly life that raises their souls above every material or psychological yoke, so that they live in obedience to their masters, lest the masters be given an opportunity to curse the new religion and the God whom they worship.

6.1.0.en: In the previous verse the Apostle spoke of the relation of slaves to their unbelieving masters, and here he speaks of the relation of slaves to their believing masters. He urges the slaves to give them full honor, because brotherhood in the faith does not mean that we deprive of honor those to whom honor is due; rather, we as slaves should serve them with greater diligence and faithfulness, because those who share in the blessings of salvation and in the communion of the Holy Sacraments are beloved believers who deserve all love and esteem from us. And Timothy is to teach and exhort these things so that doctrine may be translated into practical life and conduct.

6.1.1.en: Take care to honor those in authority, whether Christians or non-Christians, even if they are domineering and biased; by your love and longsuffering you will win everyone. Be faithful in your work and sincere in your relationships for God’s sake, whatever the mistakes of others, and so you present a living picture of the true Christian and glorify God’s name.

6.2.1.en: Strifes of words: continuing in quarrels.

6.2.2.en: St. Paul attacks the false teachers who leave the commandments of Christ and the teachings of righteousness and proclaim doctrines strange to the Church. These have fallen into pride and ignorance, and also into disputing and quarreling that breed many sins such as strife, envy and evil surmisings, and even reach to lying and slandering others, that is, they depart from love and divide the Church. And these, with their misleading, corrupt discussions, use godliness as a cover for trading in people and gaining positions and money, and they stray from true godliness. For this reason Paul warns Timothy against being troubled or having dealings with them.

6.3.0.en: Godliness from the Christian viewpoint is life with God, and it requires contentment in material things, that is, being satisfied with the material things God has bestowed on us. This is sound trade: seeking the salvation of the soul and keeping away from the love of money.

6.4.0.en: When a person is born, he has no money with him. And when he dies he takes nothing material with him, as Job said (Job 1:21). All this calls us not to cling to the love of money but to godliness and care for the spiritual life. If a person has his necessary needs of food and clothing, this suffices him to be occupied with his goal, that is, the salvation of his soul.

6.5.1.en: On the other hand, he warns the believers against the love of money and the desire for riches, for this exposes them to many temptations that lead them to perdition; for in their pursuit of riches they use wrong ways and are exposed to pride and various sins. More than this, the Apostle counts it among the mother sins that breed many evils, so that a person gives up his faith because the love of money has become his goal, and thereby his soul is tormented by the multitude of sins.

6.5.2.en: The whole world is under your feet, and you use it as you wish. But beware lest it master you and money become your goal, even under the name of raising the standard of living or acquiring modern devices, for by this you are distracted from your goal, who is God, and you gradually give up His commandments.

6.6.s.en: (3) The striving of the children of God

6.6.0.en: The spiritual person flees from the love of money and pursues holiness and righteousness, and takes care to acquire the basic Christian virtues, which are faith in the mercies of the Lord, and love, which is the main foundation of true Christian life. He practices patience in bearing trials and sufferings, and is marked by meekness of heart and of feelings in his behavior toward others.

6.7.0.en: Paul calls his disciple Timothy to hold fast to the Christian faith which he declared before the Church through his ministry and teachings, and to complete his spiritual striving for the salvation of his soul.

6.8.0.en: A good confession: here the Apostle refers to Christ’s answer to Pilate when he asked Him, “Art thou a king then?” (Jn 18:37). He said, “To this end was I born,” and, “for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth.” Likewise when they asked Him, “Art thou then the Son of God?” He answered, “Ye say that I am” (Lk 22:70). As Paul gives his disciple a weighty charge, he calls to witness God the Father, who gives life and gives resurrection from the dead, and His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, who offered Himself as an example for us in bearing witness to the truth before Pontius Pilate. And the charge he gives him is that he carry out God’s commandments and live without spot or fault that could be a cause of blame directed at him by the flock or by God on the day of judgment. And he charges him to do this until the end of his life in the world, or until the Second Coming takes place, if that happens in his lifetime.

6.9.0.en: The Second Coming of Christ will be shown by God in His appointed time, which He Himself fixed and which is known to Him alone, the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings and Lord of lords. It is to be noted that the titles mentioned here are the very titles of God the Son as they occur in (Rev 17:14, 19:16), which show His glory and His authority over all creation.

6.10.0.en: Christ has immortality, which He does not derive from anyone, and death cannot overcome Him; He dwells in the light which no man can approach unto, which even the angels cannot approach; no one has seen Him in His essence, nor can anyone see Him. We offer Him honor and the confession of His eternal power.

6.10.1.en: Care for your goal, which is eternity, where you will enjoy the vision of God and His inexpressible fellowship. Do not be lax in your striving to live righteousness, holiness and continual repentance, because the greatness of the Kingdom deserves that you labor today, for no labor can be measured against the glories of heaven.

6.11.0.en: This present world: life in the world.

6.11.1.en: Uncertain riches: that they not trust or rely on their wealth.

6.11.2.en: The Apostle charged the rich in the treasures that the world gives not to be puffed up in themselves, and not to let their possession of money drive them to excessive self-importance, and not to rely on their wealth, which they may lose in a single hour, affirming the necessity of setting all hope on God and not on money, God in whose hands is abundant good and who pours out upon us of His grace that we may enjoy His gifts.

6.12.0.en: It befits the rich to practice works of love whose credit remains forever, and to multiply good works, so that their hands give generously to the needy.

6.13.0.en: The giving of the rich lays up for them a treasure in heaven which they will enjoy, and a foundation on which they rely for entering the Kingdom.

6.13.1.en: If God has given you money or abilities, you are a steward over them, to use them in helping those around you, for by works of mercy you can enter heaven. So seize every opportunity to do good.

6.14.0.en: That which is committed to thy trust: the oral teachings that Paul taught to Timothy, which are called the tradition of the Church. The Apostle ends his epistle to his disciple, asking him to keep the living faith that was delivered to the saints and to avoid the foolish discussions of the false teachers, who exchanged faith for knowledge and so fell into falsely so called knowledge.

6.15.0.en: As some of them, like the Gnostics, claimed to have attained knowledge, they wandered in the mazes of this satanic, misleading knowledge; and while they were seeking salvation through knowledge, they failed utterly and lost the doctrine of sound faith and the knowledge of God.

6.16.0.en: The Apostle ends his epistle with the apostolic blessing and his asking grace for his disciple.

6.16.1.en: Hold fast to the teachings you hear in the Church so that you live them, and take care to know God so that you love Him, and keep away from the debates of learning that do not lead you to God, even if they are spiritual sciences.
